prompt:
Read the following email from your classmate Paul and write him a reply.

Dear Li Ming,
I was really excited to hear that you’d invite some young craftsmen to demonstrate their innovative craft-making on campus. May I know more about what they’ll show? Also, I’d like to help with your preparation work. Please let me know what I can do.
Yours,
Paul

Write your answer in about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET.
Do not use your own name in your email; use “Li Ming” instead. (10 points)
body: Thank you for your interest in the craft demonstration. Next Friday afternoon, five young craftsmen will come to our campus to show how they breathe new life into traditional crafts. For example, one will use 3D printing to design paper-cut patterns, and another will weave bamboo into stylish modern lamps. Visitors will even get the chance to try some of the skills themselves.
Your help would be greatly appreciated. Since you are good at photography, could you take pictures during the event and help design the posters this week? Please let me know if you are available.

prompt:
Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the following table. In your essay, you should
1) describe the table briefly,
2) explain its intended meaning, and
3) give your comments.
You should write neatly on the ANSWER SHEET. (20 points)

【表格】近年来全国居民平均每百户年末主要耐用消费品拥有量
年份 | 空调（台） | 洗衣机（台） | 电冰箱（台）
2014 | 75.2 | 83.7 | 85.5
2017 | 96.1 | 91.7 | 95.3
2020 | 117.7 | 96.7 | 101.8
2023 | 145.9 | 98.2 | 103.4
body: The table shows how many air conditioners, washing machines and refrigerators every 100 Chinese households owned at the end of selected years from 2014 to 2023. The most striking change is in air conditioners, whose number nearly doubled from 75.2 to 145.9. By comparison, washing machines and refrigerators grew more gradually, from 83.7 to 98.2 and from 85.5 to 103.4 respectively.

These figures clearly reflect the steady improvement in people’s living standards. With rising incomes, durable goods that were once luxuries have become everyday necessities. Since most families already own a washing machine and a refrigerator, demand for them is approaching saturation. Air conditioners, however, are still spreading fast, because many households now install one in each room in pursuit of greater comfort.

In my view, this trend is encouraging, but it also brings new challenges. More appliances mean higher energy consumption and more electronic waste. Therefore, manufacturers should develop more energy-efficient products, and consumers should use them responsibly and recycle old ones properly. Only in this way can a better life go hand in hand with a greener planet.

prompt:
Suppose you are planning a short play based on a classic Chinese novel. Write your friend John an email to:
1) introduce the play, and
2) invite him to take part in it.
Write your answer in about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET.
Do not use your own name in your email. Use “Li Ming” instead. (10 points)
body: I’m writing to tell you about a short play I’m planning. Based on the classic Chinese novel Journey to the West, it tells how the Monkey King and his companions overcome all kinds of difficulties on their way to fetch Buddhist scriptures. The play will last about 20 minutes and be performed in English at our college art festival next month.

Knowing that you love Chinese culture and have acting experience, I sincerely invite you to join us and play the role of Zhu Bajie, a funny but kind-hearted character. Rehearsals will be held every Saturday afternoon. Please let me know if you are interested.

prompt:
Write an essay based on the chart below. In your essay, you should
1) describe and interpret the chart, and
2) give your comments.
Write your answer in about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)

【图表】某社区老年人主要日常休闲活动调查（柱状图）：看电视 90.80%，散步 68.30%，养花 34.70%，阅读 31.80%，下棋 18.40%
body: The bar chart presents the results of a survey on the main leisure activities of the elderly in a community. Watching TV is by far the most popular, chosen by 90.8% of the respondents, followed by taking walks at 68.3%. In contrast, growing flowers, reading and playing chess are much less common, at 34.7%, 31.8% and 18.4% respectively.

The chart suggests that most senior citizens prefer leisure activities that are easy, inexpensive and require little physical effort. Television brings them news and entertainment at home, while walking is a simple way to keep fit. Activities that demand more energy, skills or company, such as playing chess, attract far fewer people.

In my opinion, the leisure life of the elderly should be richer. Communities could organize reading clubs, gardening classes and chess competitions, which would not only enrich their spare time but also help them stay mentally active and socially connected.
